decisions.title: Purpose and scope: a live CI fixture, eight operations
decisions.context: the skill's live layer had one credential-gated fixture (another API, on a shared free account) and one no-auth public API. Neither can prove a write live, and neither runs without a secret or a third party. Gitea is open source, ships a single static binary with an embedded SQLite database, and publishes its Swagger 2.0 description (467 operations), so CI can start a real instance, seed it, mint a token and run every selected operation — reads and a write — against it in about ten seconds, with nothing shared and nothing to leak.

resolution.decision: select eight operations over four resources: server version (`GET /version`), repositories (`GET /repos/search`, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}`), issues (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`, `GET …/issues/{index}`, `POST …/issues`), users (`GET /user`, `GET /users/{username}`). Exclude the remaining 459 with the single reason "pilot scope (D-0001)"; the eleven the reader marks unsupported (binary and text bodies, multipart uploads) carry its reason instead.
resolution.note: Alternatives: a Docker image (rejected: the CI runner and the sandbox both run the binary directly, and Docker is not available in the sandbox); a hosted Gitea such as Codeberg (rejected: a third party's production service and a shared account, which is what this fixture exists to avoid).

decisions.question: What does the live CI fixture run, and against what?

choices.label: A Gitea binary CI starts and seeds itself; eight operations over four resources
A Docker image
A hosted Gitea such as Codeberg

decisions.title: Envelopes and pagination
decisions.context: `GET /version` wraps one string as `{version}`; `GET /repos/search` wraps its page as `{ok, data: [...]}`; every other selected response is the bare object or array. Gitea paginates with `page`/`limit` query parameters and reports totals in `X-Total-Count` and `Link` headers, which a connector selection cannot read.

resolution.decision: `gitea_version` returns the bare `String` (`$.version`); `gitea_searchRepos` keeps its envelope as `Gitea_RepositorySearchResult { ok, data }` because `ok` carries information; `gitea_listIssues` returns `[Gitea_Issue]`. Both lists expose `page` and `limit`; there is no `more`/`total` field to map, so callers page until a short page.
resolution.note: Alternatives: a synthetic page type with the header-derived total (rejected: not expressible in connect v0.3).

decisions.question: Which response envelopes are kept?

choices.label: searchRepos keeps {ok, data}; version and the issue list are bare
Flatten searchRepos to [Gitea_Repository] too

decisions.title: Enums keep Gitea's wire casing; `StateType` becomes an enum
decisions.context: the spec types issue and milestone `state` as a bare string (`StateType`) although the API only sends `open` and `closed`; the `state` filter parameter is enumerated `closed`, `open`, `all` and the `type` filter `issues`, `pulls`. All are already valid GraphQL enum names.

resolution.decision: `Gitea_StateType { open closed }` for the fields, `Gitea_IssueStateFilter { open closed all }` and `Gitea_IssueType { issues pulls }` for the arguments, all in wire casing so they serialise straight into query strings with no `->match` table. The conformance oracle checks the JSON body against the spec's `string`, so the tighter GraphQL type costs nothing there; a third state value would surface as a GraphQL enum error, which is the right place to learn about it.
resolution.note: Alternatives: `state: String` (rejected: an enum documents the vocabulary and MCP tool descriptions benefit).

decisions.question: Are issue and milestone `state` and the issue filters enums?

choices.label: Enums in wire casing: Gitea_StateType, Gitea_IssueStateFilter, Gitea_IssueType
state: String, as the spec types StateType

decisions.title: Error mapping
decisions.context: probed live (memory.md): 404 is `{"errors": null, "message": "not found", "url": ".../api/swagger"}`, 401 is `{"message": "token is required", "url": ...}`, 422 is `{"message": "[Title]: Required", "url": ...}`. `errors` is present only on some statuses and null when present.

resolution.decision: `message: $($.message ?? 'Gitea request failed')`, extensions `httpStatus: $status` and `details: $.errors`. `url` is the Swagger UI link and is not mapped.

decisions.question: What do Gitea's error bodies map to?

choices.label: message (default 'Gitea request failed'), with httpStatus and details extensions; url not mapped
The same, plus the Swagger UI url as an extension

decisions.title: Repository field exclusions
decisions.context: the full `Repository` carries seven `allow_*` merge switches plus `default_merge_style`, `default_delete_branch_after_merge`, `default_allow_maintainer_edit`, `autodetect_manual_merge` and `ignore_whitespace_conflicts` (merge-strategy configuration), `internal_tracker`/`external_tracker`/`external_wiki` (integration settings), `mirror_interval`/`mirror_updated`, a recursive `parent` and a `repo_transfer` in progress.

resolution.decision: exclude those nineteen on both repository operations (listed per operation in selection.yaml); map the other forty-six, typed. Nothing kept is a JSON scalar.
resolution.note: Alternatives: map everything (rejected: merge configuration is repository administration, not graph data, and `parent` recurses).

decisions.question: Are Repository's merge-strategy, integration and mirror settings exposed?

choices.label: The nineteen excluded on both repository operations; the other forty-six mapped, typed
Everything mapped

decisions.title: Comma-separated filters stay `String`
decisions.context: `GET …/issues` takes `labels` and `milestones` as comma-separated names in one query parameter; the spec types them `string`, not `array`.

resolution.decision: expose them as `String` and pass them through. A list argument would need a `->joinNotNull(",")` mapping and would still be the same wire value.
resolution.note: Alternatives: `[String!]` with a join (deferred: revisit when the list-argument lint rule wants an e2e case proving the join).

decisions.question: How are the comma-separated `labels` and `milestones` filters exposed?

choices.label: String, passed through
[String!] joined by the connector

decisions.title: `createIssue` is a Mutation with flat scalar arguments
decisions.context: `POST …/issues` is the one write in scope. Its body `CreateIssueOption` is flat already: `title` (required), `body`, `assignees[]` (logins), `labels[]` (label ids), `milestone` (id), `due_date`, `ref`, `closed`, and a deprecated single `assignee`.
decisions.question: How is createIssue exposed?

choices.label: A Mutation with flat scalar arguments, tagged write
A Mutation taking an input object mirroring the body

resolution.note: Alternatives: an input object mirroring the body (rejected: flat arguments keep the write expressible in `rover connector test`, which never builds an object-valued argument into the request body). Amended 2026-09-30 (D-0019 to D-0025): the constructor does not drop null arguments; the router sends an explicit null as JSON null (measured by create_issue_nulls). What drops a null is `$args.x?` on the body member, which also drops an absent argument and nothing else -- an empty string, empty list, false and zero go through. The minimal call sends {title} alone only because absent arguments are left out. Amended 2026-10-05 (reopened and resolved again): the mutation no longer carries `@tag(name: "write")`, and selection.yaml no longer lists `tags: [write]`. This target applies `@tag` only when the user's supergraph uses GraphOS Contracts, with the names those contracts already filter on, and this pilot's supergraph has none; the `flat` choice's label still reads 'tagged write' as it was offered on 2026-09-10. The shape (flat scalar arguments) is unchanged.
resolution.decision: `gitea_createIssue(owner!, repo!, title!, body, assignees: [String!], labels: [ID!], milestone: ID, dueDate, ref, closed)` → `Gitea_Issue`, with no `@tag`. The body maps each argument by name; the constructor drops null arguments, so the minimal call sends `{title}` alone (asserted at unit and e2e). `assignee` is not exposed.

decisions.title: The live layer runs the write too
decisions.context: the other pilots keep writes WireMock-only because the live target is a shared account or a third party. This fixture's live target is an instance CI created seconds earlier and discards at the end of the job.

resolution.decision: `tests/live.yaml` covers all eight operations; `create_issue` runs live with `safety: write` and asserts the created issue's title and open state. Ids and index numbers are fixed by the seed (`fixture/fixture-repo`, issue 1) so single-object reads can run live without chaining a previous response.

decisions.question: Does the live layer run the write?

choices.label: Yes: create_issue runs live against the instance CI created
No: writes stay WireMock-only, as on the other pilots

decisions.title: Conformance waivers: the undocumented 404 and 422 bodies
decisions.context: `factory validate` reports 2 bodies as unchecked: tests/fixtures/mappings/repo_not_found.json (the spec documents no body shape for get:/repos/{owner}/{repo} → 404) and tests/fixtures/mappings/create_issue_invalid.json (none for post:/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues → 422). Gitea's Swagger declares both responses (`notFound`, `validationError`) without a schema.

resolution.decision: both bodies were recorded from the seeded instance on 2026-09-10 and the e2e cases assert the error mapping built on them (D-0004), so the gap is the spec's, not the fixture's. Recorded as two waivers in selection.yaml (status unchecked, `until` Gitea documents the response bodies): validate reports them as waived with this reason; lint reports either waiver once nothing has that status there any more, or when it expires.
resolution.note: Alternatives: patch the spec with the observed shape (rejected: a patch asserts what the API guarantees, and one observation of an error body is not that; a waiver says only that the gap is known); leave them `unchecked` (rejected: the report would carry the same two lines forever with nobody on record as having looked).

decisions.question: What happens to the two undocumented 404 and 422 bodies validate cannot judge?

choices.label: Waive them as unchecked until Gitea documents the bodies
Patch the spec with the observed shape
Leave them unchecked

decisions.title: Scalar choice for the 19 int64-backed slots the int-overflow lint reports
decisions.question: Gitea declares 155 numeric properties as format: int64. GraphQL Int is 32-bit. Which of the 19 selected Int-typed slots become String, which become ID, and which keep Int?
decisions.context: factory lint pilots/gitea reported 19 int-overflow errors: 18 response leaves and the index argument of gitea_issue. Gitea itself declares no minimum or maximum on any numeric property, so the format hint is the only fact available.
affects: 15 counter fields on Gitea_User, Gitea_Repository, Gitea_Milestone, Gitea_Attachment and Gitea_Issue

resolution.note: Alternatives: keep the counters Int behind a doc comment saying the value fits in Int (rejected: it invents a suppression mechanism the task's pre-decisions explicitly forbade, and a sentence beside a field does not change what the router coerces; it also left 15 of 19 findings cleared by prose rather than by a fix). Type Gitea_Issue.number as ID for symmetry with the argument (rejected: the pre-decided policy names ID for id, *Id and *_id only, and an output ID is emitted by this router as a bare JSON number, so it would not carry the String contract the other 17 fields now carry). Map with $(path?->jsonStringify ?? null), which preserves null identically (rejected: reconcile::parse_selection does not read a $(...) expression block as a mapping of its path, so all 77 converted leaves were reported as 'renamed by the selection but the connector does not map it' and 'selection says all fields; N not mapped' — the ->match form keeps reconcile clean). Pin the null behaviour with unit cases in this workspace's own tests/gitea.connector.yaml (rejected on measurement, see the decision). Waive the findings (rejected: selection.schema.json $defs/waiver carries only the conformance statuses unchecked and unmatched, and lint has no waiver mechanism at all).
resolution.decision: All 18 int64-backed response leaves become String, mapped with path->match([null, null], [@, @->jsonStringify]): the three magnitudes (Gitea_Repository.size kilobytes, Gitea_Attachment.size bytes, Gitea_Issue.timeEstimate seconds) and the 15 counters alike, per the pre-decided pilot fix policy. The index argument of gitea_issue becomes ID!, matching uid, priorityOwnerId, teamId and starredBy on gitea_searchRepos; ID input coercion takes an integer literal, so tests/cases/issue.graphql and tests/live/issue.graphql keep index: 1 unchanged. The null guard is not decoration: a bare ->jsonStringify turns a JSON null into the 4-character string "null". THIS WORKSPACE DOES NOT PIN THAT, and cannot: unit cases feeding a JSON null into the converted fields were written and then removed, because every apiResponseBody here is also a conformance body and Gitea's swagger declares all eighteen properties non-nullable — one such case, measured on a throwaway copy, takes validate from "23 bodies conform, 0 do not" to "22 bodies conform, 1 do not" with "$.followers_count: null is not allowed (shape is not nullable)" and exit 1. tests/gitea.connector.yaml therefore carries 9 cases and no null body, and unguarding the mappings leaves it green — measured: rewriting all 77 ->match(...) mappings back to a bare ->jsonStringify on a throwaway copy still gives "TEST RESULTS: SUCCESSFUL 46 passed; 0 failed", exit 0. The proof lives outside the pilot, in .github/scripts/null-mapping-probe.sh, run by CI's stack job on a throwaway workspace nobody validates: guarded "TEST RESULTS: SUCCESSFUL 8 passed; 0 failed", bare ->jsonStringify "TEST RESULTS: FAILED 7 passed; 1 failed" with the actual carrying "bytes": "null". Before touching these 18 fields, read that script — not this suite. What this workspace does prove: unit 46 passed, 0 failed; e2e 11 passed, 0 failed through a real router; validate 23 conform, 0 do not, 0 unchecked, 2 waived. tests/live.yaml's four numeric predicates now pipe through tonumber, which fails loudly on a non-number, where a bare >= on a JSON string compares as a string and is true for every value the API will ever send.

decisions.title: Enable verbose per-field doc comments (opt-in evaluation)

choices.label: Add per-field doc comments sourced from the inventory description facts
Keep root-field/type-only doc comments (repo default)

resolution.note: A stakeholder comparison against the output of an earlier deterministic generator found this schema missing most field-level doc comments that generator always emitted. The source descriptions are already captured in the inventory (55% of gitea properties); nothing surfaced them. Opting gitea in as the worked proof pending a real success-rate/cost comparison.
resolution.decision: Opt gitea into per-field doc comments as the worked example of opt-in object field doc comments (references/schema-authoring.md § Object field descriptions); not defaulted on repo-wide until measured.

decisions.title: Enable one-sentence source descriptions on arguments (opt-in evaluation)

choices.label: Add the inventory parameter description, cut to one sentence, in front of the argument constraint clause
Constraint clause and pagination wording only (repo default)

resolution.note: The 2026-09-22 AppWorld LLM-arm bundle carried 1,565 argument doc comments where the 16 September bundle carried 0 (fix-list finding D1). 448 were rule-driven — 308 argument constraint clauses, 140 § Pagination wording — and 1,058 had no rule asking for them: 691 verbatim OpenAPI parameter text, 367 per-argument access_token sentences from the authoring brief. The bundle's description text went from 28 KB to 229 KB across every doc-comment surface, not arguments alone. The rule that followed makes the source sentence opt-in per service, one sentence, never type or requiredness (references/schema-authoring.md § Argument descriptions); the argument constraint clause stays default-on. Opting gitea in as the worked proof pending a measured comparison, as D-0014 did for object fields.
resolution.decision: Opt gitea into one-sentence source descriptions on root-field arguments as the worked example of opt-in argument source descriptions: 30 arguments gain the inventory description cut to one sentence, verbatim, as a single-line string. The four page/limit arguments keep § Pagination's wording only (they carry none today, and the two pre-existing pagination-bounds-unknown warnings stay). mode, sort, order, state and type keep their existing curated doc comments — the rule fills gaps and does not relitigate curation. labels and milestone on createIssue get none, because 'list of label ids' and 'milestone id' add nothing to what [ID!] and ID already say; 'search string' on listIssues(q:) stays, because q alone does not say the value is a search term. title, body, assignees and ref have no source description. Not defaulted on repo-wide until measured.

decisions.title: The pilot's one relationship field: Gitea_RepositoryMeta.ownerUser via get:/users/{username}
decisions.question: Which of the inventory's candidate_entity_link facts becomes the relationship field CI runs through unit, e2e and live on every PR?
decisions.context: inventory links reports 8 candidates on 6 shapes. selection draft --links proposes only Organization > username, and that host is reachable only through Repository.repo_transfer, which the selection excludes and the seed leaves null. Email, TrackedTime, PayloadUser and Activity are returned by no included operation; Email > username and TrackedTime > user_name would need a new operation (get:/user/emails) or a new seed write (tracked time). RepositoryMeta > owner is reachable from two included reads (Issue.repository on get:/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues and .../issues/{index}) and the seed's issue #1 carries owner = fixture, but the fact targets get:/packages/{owner}, a list_context:true list of packages, not a GET-by-id.

choices.label: RepositoryMeta > owner resolved through get:/users/{username} (entry corrects the fact's target)
Email > username, adding get:/user/emails to the selection
Organization > username, including Repository.repo_transfer
TrackedTime > user_name, adding a tracked-time read and a seed write

resolution.note: Alternatives: email-username (rejected: adds a ninth operation, its own unit/e2e/live/conformance obligations, to carry a link whose every row points at the token's own user); org-username (rejected: repo_transfer is null in the seed so the field never resolves live, and Organization.username is the org's own name, a self-reference); tracked-time (rejected: needs a new read and a seed write the live layer would depend on). The same judgement records that the candidate heuristic matched owner to the packages list route, a false target the entry overrides.
resolution.decision: Link Gitea_RepositoryMeta.owner (the owner's login) to Query.gitea_user's get:/users/{username} as the field ownerUser. It is semantically a foreign key (Gitea answers GET /users/{name} for the user or organisation that owns the repository), it needs no new operation and no seed change, the seed's issue #1 reaches it live (repository.owner = fixture), and ownerUser avoids field-exists on the existing owner scalar. The links entry names operation get:/users/{username} and parameter username in place of the fact's get:/packages/{owner}: the fact's target is a list_context:true list endpoint, not the owner's by-id read.

decisions.title: RepositoryMeta > owner stays a confirmed link after the link-target rule removed its fact; the null guard is pasted
decisions.question: Since crate 0.5.51 the link-target rule keeps a GET-by-id as a link target only when its response carries the path parameter's key; Gitea's User spells it login, so inventory links now lists 0 candidates and refuses get:/users/{username}. Does D-0017's link survive, and in what form?
decisions.context: inventory build is byte-identical to the committed inventory.json (#133 regenerated it). inventory links: 0 candidate links, 5 GET-by-id refused, get:/users/{username}: its response carries no username of the parameter's type. lint raises no link-* error for an entry with no backing fact and reconcile reports links =1 in sync; lint warned link-null-guard because Gitea_RepositoryMeta.owner is a nullable String. No other included GET-by-id qualifies under the new rule. Measured with curl against the seeded Gitea 1.25.0: GET /api/v1/users/fixture returns login fixture, and GET /api/v1/users/ (the empty segment a null owner produces) returns 404 text/plain 404 page not found.

choices.label: Keep the link as a judgement (selection is judgements); re-print through links apply --dry-run with the null guard; add the null-parent e2e case
Remove the link; gitea carries no relationship field again
Switch to a link the new rule still proposes (none exists: 0 candidates)

resolution.note: drop rejected: the pilot is CI's only executed relationship field, and nothing about the API changed. other-link rejected: the new rule proposes none. The null-parent item is hand-built from the issue.json recording; the seed never returns a null owner, so the live layer proves only the non-null parent.
resolution.decision: Keep RepositoryMeta > owner -> get:/users/{username} (field ownerUser) confirmed. The link was never backed by a fact for this target (D-0017 already overrode the fact's get:/packages/{owner}), and the login spelling is a known limitation of the rule, not evidence against the relationship: Gitea's GET /users/{username} returns the user whose login equals the username, which the live case asserts (ownerUser.login == owner). owner is nullable, so the field is re-printed by links apply --dry-run with its isSuccess and selection null guard and pasted verbatim, and a null-parent e2e case (issue #3, whose repository omits owner: the spec does not require it and allows no null string) proves the guard; user_empty_segment.json answers the GET /users/ the router still sends for the null parent (the guard maps the answer, it does not skip the request) as Gitea does (404) and is waived as unmatched, since no operation describes that request.

decisions.title: createIssue(body): an explicit null is omitted from the body
decisions.context: The write-body proof asks what the connector sends when body is passed as an explicit null. Measured 2026-09-30: without a guard the router sent "body": null (the spec documents the member as non-nullable). The body member is now written `$args.body?`, which drops the key when the argument is null; tests/cases/create_issue_nulls.graphql reaches WireMock with the key absent and its stub demands exactly that. D-0007's remark that the constructor drops null arguments is now true for an explicit null as well as for an argument left out.

resolution.note: Omitting is what the spec asks for. Real Gitea 1.25.0 (seeded fixture, 2026-09-30) also accepted a POST carrying every nullable member as null (201, each left at its default), so omission changes no outcome; it only stops the connector sending a body the spec says is invalid.
resolution.decision: omit for body. Gitea treats a null body as no description and stores an empty string, the same as leaving it out.
